update.title: M08 pride: 10.15 Pride written, angles woven, pride passages anchored in the register
update.strand: pride and arrogance (M08): pride, boasting, mocking (#2156)
update.researcher_instruction: "ensure all the verses that need a re-read, or incorporation into another cluster read as outstanding items in the register, then proceed with a consolidated cross batch synergy, updating the claims register, weaving and cross checking that the narrative is anchored in the claims register for this group of words" (2026-10-15); earlier: "group B - lets do one more scan of these, it seems they are mostly data.  Set them aside as data unless the terms are supporting other M-codes"; "mark the 34 verses forward as suggested. then start reading A, C and D in batches.  The Ch 13 references should include a reflection on a) are any of the pride words indicative of their characteristics? I suspect there is difference between the 'pride','most high' of God, which is not an assumed position but a undisputed state, verses IB pride that is mostly assumed."
update.method: M08 overview; group B (height words, 211 verses) scanned: 135 data, 42 pride sense, 34 forward (OT-97). Groups A, C, D with the B pride-sense verses and E read in five batches by passage (355 verses: 312 read, 25 carried from M09, 18 data), each with a Ch 13 reflection; Isa 47:8 read from group F. Outstanding items registered as OT-107 (#2157), OT-97.25 and OT-103.22 closed, OT-105 items added. Cross-batch account (m08-pride-synergy). New 10.15 Pride holds the full account (#1961); angles woven in context into 13.1 (Majesty), 10.2 (Pride and hearing), 10.10 (Pride over another), 10.7 (Presumption), Ch 11 s4 (Lifted up); pointers in Ch 12, 10.14, 10.0. Anchor cross-check: every narrative passage using a pride-group word read against the register (151 before the weave, 110 telling no claim); the pride statements among them registered or told; the passages that use a pride word for another concept left to that concept's strand.
update.claims_changed_note: 31 new claims (10.15, 13.1, Ch 11 lexical); existing claims C-182, C-207, C-208, C-209, C-210 and 2-2 told in further passages; no claim withdrawn
update.not_woven_note: Held for other strands (OT-107): 13.2 (2Pe 2:10-11; Job 33:23), 13.3 (2Co 12:7; 1Ti 3:6), 13.4 (Job 41:34; Job 38:11; Psa 89:9), the 25 God-on-high height verses, the self-exaltation words outside M08 (H7311A, G5312, H5375L, H7682), H2778A, the M06 scorn words, G2754, G1703, pride against love/mourning/rest for M51/M03/M33, the Ch 12 Held vice lists, Amo 8:7 and Job 9:23 unsettled. Ch 1 outline (#2111) not touched.
update.structure_change: New sub-chapter 10.15 Pride (reading order 26, after 10.14; later chapters +1). New sections: 13.1 Majesty (before Lowering himself); 10.2 Pride and hearing; 10.10 Pride over another; 10.7 Presumption (before Willing). Ch 11 s4 gains the face Lifted up. Ch 12 Pride section points to 10.15; 10.14 opening and Connections name 10.15; 10.0 names 10.12 to 10.15.
update.structure_reason: Pride has its own words, faces, other parties and outcomes across the activities, with God as its counter-measure; a key characteristic gets one full account as its own Ch 10 sub-chapter (#1961), with each angle woven in context (#1920). Ch 12 keeps the passages that show the inner being going wrong.
update.quote_note: every double-quoted part of 10.15 (149) and of the lines added to the eight woven chapters (65), split on the ellipsis, checked against iba.db verse text in canonical order (m08-narrative-quote-check-v1-20261015.py)
update.notes: The 10.15 chapter row was added directly to narrative_chapter (reading_order 26, later chapters +1), as for 10.14, because no Narrative-Register action adds a chapter (#2155).

new.text: The same Hebrew words name God's majesty and human pride; the English marks the difference, not the Hebrew
new.beyond_text: compares the renderings of one word family across the verses

new.text: Pride, the boast and the mock belong together in the verses
new.beyond_text: groups three word families as one subject

new.text: Pride holds as its own what was given: strength, healing, majesty, wealth, beauty and height are given, and the heart rises on them
new.beyond_text: reads the accounts side by side as one order, with 1Co 4:7 as its plain statement

new.text: Pride credits to its own hand what was done through it
new.beyond_text: reads the rod's boast with the axe saying of the same passage, and Nebuchadnezzar's boast

new.text: The same word names an honour God chooses, gives or restores, and what was given can be turned into pride
new.beyond_text: sets the honour given beside the given turned to pride

new.text: Pride at its full height says of itself what is true only of God: the proud city's "I am, and there is no one besides me" repeats God's self-statement
new.beyond_text: sets Isa 47:8, 10 and Zep 2:15 beside Isa 45:5 and 46:9

new.text: Pride claims a place that is God's: likeness to the Most High, a god's seat, his temple
new.beyond_text: joins three claims to God's place

new.text: Pride deceives the one who holds it, and the fear one inspires in others can feed it
new.beyond_text: reads Obd 3 with Jer 49:16

new.text: Pride shuts God out of the thoughts, is set against faith, and gives no rest
new.beyond_text: joins Psa 10:4 and Hab 2:4-5

new.text: Pride shows in the eyes, the walk and what is worn, and the verses join it to ease
new.beyond_text: gathers the outward signs and the ease named beside them

new.text: Pride is set against hearing: it will not take rebuke or advice, and the scoffer is known by what he will not receive
new.beyond_text: gathers the pride and scoffer sayings with the hearing named against them

new.text: Presumption acts on its own word where another word was given: speaking what God did not command, going up when told not to, not keeping the decision given
new.beyond_text: reads the presumption verses as one act; reads Deu 1:41-43 as presumption in the words of repentance

new.text: God works to keep pride from a person: by warnings that open the ear, and by a thorn given against conceit
new.beyond_text: joins Job 33:16-17 and 2Co 12:7-9

new.text: What the verses set against pride is hearing and the fear of God
new.beyond_text: names the opposite the verses give

new.text: Pride stands over someone: the poor, the widow, the needy left unaided, the righteous; it closes the heart to pity and is set against love
new.beyond_text: gathers who pride stands over in the verses

new.text: Pride is also felt by the one under it, and the answer given is to look to the Lord
new.beyond_text: reads Psa 123:4 with 123:2

new.text: The verses do not condemn boasting as such; they judge it by what it rests on
new.beyond_text: compares the boasts judged and the boasts commanded

new.text: Boasting in oneself is excluded because what is held was given: grace, gift, and God's choosing of the low
new.beyond_text: gives the ground of the exclusion

new.text: Boasting in weakness claims no more than is so, and makes room for Christ's power
new.beyond_text: reads 2Co 12:6 against pride's standing

new.text: The right measure of oneself, and of one's boast, is the measure God assigned; thinking oneself something when one is nothing is self-deception
new.beyond_text: joins the measure of thinking and of boasting

new.text: A boast can be in another person, and it puts the one who boasts at stake on the other's conduct
new.beyond_text: reads Paul's boasts of the churches

new.text: Mocking takes the sufferer's trust in God as its target, and the sufferer answers God, not the mockers
new.beyond_text: reads the taunt of Psa 22:8 with 22:9 and its use at the cross

new.text: Mocking God's messengers and word goes on until there is no remedy; the same call is met by mocking and by humbling
new.beyond_text: reads 2Ch 36:16 as the end of the way back, beside 2Ch 30:10-11

new.text: In the proverbs pride brings its own fall, with no other hand named; elsewhere God brings it down
new.beyond_text: compares the sayings with no agent and the verses that name God

new.text: The one who is high by nature comes near the low; those who make themselves high are known from afar
new.beyond_text: reads the contrast of Psa 138:6

new.text: The charge of pride can come from another's anger or from a ready explanation, and the verses do not make it true
new.beyond_text: reads Eliab's charge against the chapter, and Eliphaz's explanation against the book

new.text: The same words are not pride when the height is given or faces God: a heart lifted up in God's ways, strength of soul given, a heart not lifted up and at rest
new.beyond_text: sets the other face of the words beside their proud uses

new.text: God's majesty is his own and everlasting, shown in what he does, turned toward help, and joined to what only he does
new.beyond_text: gathers what the majesty verses say of it

new.text: God's majesty is challenged and not overturned; his laughter answers only those who rise against him and is never aimed at the weak
new.beyond_text: compares God's derision with human mocking

new.text: The Son's majesty is received and grounded, stands beside his being handed over, and does not defend itself against mockery; he did not grasp what pride grasps
new.beyond_text: reads the majesty, mocking and Php 2:6 verses together

new.text: One Hebrew word, ebrah, names the overflow of anger and the overflow of pride
new.beyond_text: lexical: the same word in Job 40:11 and Proverbs 21:24
sources: lexical: H5678 ebrah, Job 40:11 "overflowings", Proverbs 21:24 "pride" (iba.db verse_lexical)
